body:
The shadow-tip method is a way to find east and west in daylight without a magnetic compass. The US Army Survival Manual (FM 3-05.70) describes it as a reliable direction finder. It needs only a straight stick, a patch of level ground and some time.

Start by planting the straight stick vertically in level ground that is free of brush. Mark the exact tip of the stick's shadow with a small peg or a stone. This is your first mark.

Next, wait. The manual says to wait 15 to 30 minutes, until the shadow tip has moved several inches. Then mark the new position of the shadow tip with a second peg or stone.

Draw a straight line on the ground between the two marks. This line runs east to west. The first mark indicates west and the second mark indicates east. The manual explains that this works because the sun moves east to west across the sky.

This entry is based on a single source excerpt. The method needs a shadow sharp enough to mark, and enough waiting for the tip to move a visible distance. The excerpt does not say how accurate the line is at different times of day, in different seasons or at different latitudes.

sources.title: US Army Survival Manual FM 3-05.70 — Direction Finding

summary: Plant a straight stick upright in level ground, mark the tip of its shadow, wait 15 to 30 minutes and mark the tip again. A line between the two marks runs east to west, with the first mark on the west side and the second on the east.
title: Find east and west with a stick's shadow
